audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer states outright: 'your ball is not a projectile, so his Wind Wall (W) does nothing to your Q, W or R - a huge tempo win', repeated in 'early' ('his Wind Wall can't stop your harass at any point in the game') and in wants.you[0]. The full layer's own tldr says the opposite: 'Wind Wall eats the ball mid-flight'.
audit.why: The Orianna kit flags Q (Command: Attack, 815, 7/6/5/4/3s) as projectile, 'can be blocked by Wind Wall-class effects', and Yasuo's W (25/23/21/19/17s, 4s duration) as blocksProjectiles: 'deletes enemy projectile damage entirely'. W (Dissonance) and R (Command: Shockwave) carry no projectile flag — they detonate at the ball's position, so they are unaffected once the ball is already placed. The page was telling a paying reader to throw the ball into the wall.
audit.corrected: Q is blocked by Wind Wall; place the ball around the wall or on yourself, and once it is out there Dissonance and Shockwave still fire from it. Poke on the wall's downtime (25s at rank 1, 17s at rank 5).
sources: brief calibration note on Azir vs Yasuo Wind Wall

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer gives Yasuo all seven rows; content and packet read Orianna / Skill x5 / Orianna.
audit.why: 50.36% over 2659 games is an even lane, and the content whys already describe an even skirmish decided by E-dash discipline. The full layer is the outlier.
audit.corrected: phases[0].side -> Orianna, phases[1..5].side -> Skill with each why rewritten to an even, cooldown-grounded reason, phases[6].side -> Orianna with the why grounded in single-target dive vs AoE peel.

notes: The Wind Wall claim was the serious one: the content layer told the reader Wind Wall does nothing to any Orianna ability, while the same page's tldr said the wall eats the ball. The kit settles it — Q carries the projectile/blockable flag, W and R do not. I did not assert anything about Command: Protect (E) through the wall: the kit gives E no projectile flag but Riot's text describes the ball travelling to an ally, and that interaction is not in the data. diff 'HARD' / 8/10 sits against a 50.36% win rate and a level chart that is even in five of seven rows; the rating was left alone rather than guessed — see questionsForUser.
